intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that spermatogenic failure-105 (SPGF105) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the ADGB gene (614630) on chromosome 6q24.3.

checks.claim: Spermatogenic failure-105 (SPGF105) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the ADGB gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We found one homozygous frameshift ADGB variant (NM_024694.4: c.2801_2802del:p.K934Rfs*33), one homozygous missense ADGB variant (NM_024694.4: c.C3167T:p.T1056I), and one compound heterozygous ADGB variant
checks.explanation: The paper reports homozygous and compound heterozygous ADGB variants as causing asthenoteratozoospermia and male infertility. It does not use the SPGF105 designation.

checks.claim: The ADGB gene is located on chromosome 6q24.3.
checks.evidence_quote: Whole-exome sequencing identifies ADGB as a novel causative gene for male infertility in humans
checks.explanation: Supported only because the gene's chromosomal location counts as standard nomenclature. The abstract does not give the location.

paragraphs.text: Spermatogenic failure-105 (SPGF105) is an autosomal recessive form of male infertility. Affected men have reduced sperm motility and abnormal sperm morphology (asthenozoospermia or asthenoteratozoospermia), with malformations of the sperm acrosome and flagellum. Severe oligozoospermia has also been reported. Fertilization and pregnancy have been achieved by intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI).

checks.claim: Spermatogenic failure-105 (SPGF105) is an autosomal recessive form of male infertility.
checks.evidence_quote: we reported the identification of bi-allelic deleterious variants of ADGB in three infertile men from unrelated families using whole-exome sequencing
checks.explanation: Bi-allelic variants fit recessive inheritance, but the abstract does not explicitly say autosomal recessive.

checks.claim: Men affected with SPGF105 have reduced sperm motility and abnormal sperm morphology (asthenozoospermia or asthenoteratozoospermia).
checks.evidence_quote: Variants in the androglobin (ADGB) gene were identified in an infertile male characterized by asthenozoospermia.
checks.explanation: Asthenozoospermia (reduced motility) is supported; abnormal sperm morphology/asthenoteratozoospermia in humans is not mentioned in the abstract.

checks.claim: Men affected with SPGF105 have malformations of the sperm acrosome and flagellum.
checks.evidence_quote: the spermatozoa from patients harboring ADGB variants showed multiple acrosome and flagellum malformations under light and electron microscopy
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

checks.claim: Severe oligozoospermia has been reported in SPGF105.
checks.evidence_quote: 该患者精液分析提示严重特发性少弱畸精子症（oligoasthenoteratozoospermia, OAT）（浓度：2.0×106 mL－1
checks.explanation: A severe OAT phenotype with a sperm concentration of 2.0 x 10^6/mL fits severe oligozoospermia.

checks.claim: Fertilization and pregnancy have been achieved by intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) in SPGF105.
checks.evidence_quote: The patient carrying the pathogenic ADGB mutation achieved a successful pregnancy through intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) treatment.
checks.explanation: ICSI led to a successful pregnancy.

paragraphs.text: Wang et al. (2026) reported a Chinese man with primary infertility and severe idiopathic oligoasthenoteratozoospermia. His sperm concentration was 2.0 x 10(6)/mL, fewer than 1% of sperm showed progressive motility, no sperm had normal morphology, and sperm vitality was 16%. Sperm head abnormalities included microcephaly and conical heads. Tail defects included short, angled, coiled, and absent tails. On transmission electron microscopy, spermatozoa showed loss of the acrosome, a disorganized helical structure of the mitochondrial sheath, and disrupted or partially absent '9+2' microtubule structures in the axoneme. His reproductive hormone levels were normal, his karyotype was 46,XY, and he had no Y-chromosome microdeletion.

paragraphs.text: Gao et al. (2025) performed whole-exome sequencing in 105 Han Chinese men with idiopathic asthenoteratozoospermia and found biallelic ADGB mutations in 3 infertile men from unrelated families. One man was homozygous for a frameshift mutation (c.2801_2802del; K934Rfs*33). A second man was homozygous for a thr1056-to-ile (T1056I) missense mutation. A third man was compound heterozygous for the T1056I mutation and an ala1066-to-val (A1066V) missense mutation. All of the variants were rare in the general population, and multiple bioinformatics tools predicted them to be damaging.

paragraphs.text: Wang et al. (2026) performed whole-exome sequencing in 781 Chinese men with primary infertility and found 148 ADGB variants. They classified 6 of these as likely pathogenic, and 2 of the 6 occurred together in a single man with oligoasthenoteratozoospermia. Sanger sequencing showed that this man was compound heterozygous for 2 missense mutations in the ADGB gene: arg1620-to-gln (R1620Q) and lys1661-to-glu (K1661E). On Western blot, ADGB protein was absent from the patient's sperm. On immunofluorescence, both ADGB and the acrosome marker PNA were reduced. In normal sperm, ADGB was enriched in the acrosome and in the mitochondrial sheath of the flagellum. In the human testis, ADGB expression was low before puberty and increased after puberty. ADGB was enriched in spermatocytes and spermatids and localized to the acrosome and flagella.

paragraphs.text: In a Chinese man with severe oligoasthenoteratozoospermia (SPGF105), Wang et al. (2026) identified compound heterozygous mutations in the ADGB gene (NM_024694.4). One was a c.4859G-A transition, resulting in an arg1620-to-gln (R1620Q) substitution. The other was a c.4981A-G transition, resulting in a lys1661-to-glu (K1661E) substitution. The mutations were found by whole-exome sequencing and confirmed by Sanger sequencing. ADGB protein was absent from the patient's sperm on Western blot. His sperm showed acrosome loss, a disorganized mitochondrial sheath, and disrupted axonemes.
